question.text: A point source of light is placed at the centre of curvature of a hemispherical surface. The source emits a power of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>24</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">W</mi></math>. The radius of curvature of hemisphere is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> and the inner surface is completely reflecting. The force on the hemisphere due to the light falling on it is ______ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi></math>.

solution.text:
For completely reflecting surface, force, F=2IAc, where, I=PSurface area is intensity of radiation, A is surface area and c is speed of light.

F=2IcπR2=2P04πR2πR2c

=P02c=242×3×108=4×10-8 N
